recipes.title: Chicken Katsu
recipes.dish_alt: Sliced golden panko-crusted chicken katsu fanned on a plate with shredded cabbage and rice
recipes.prep_alt: Panko-breaded chicken cutlets ready for frying

sections.heading: Steps
items: Lay the chicken breast flat on a cutting board. If it's thick on one side, ask an adult to help slice it horizontally into a thinner, even piece, or gently pound it with the flat side of a heavy pan until it's about as thick as your thumb.
Sprinkle both sides with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with beaten egg, one with panko breadcrumbs.
Dip the chicken in flour, then egg, then press it into the panko, turning and patting so breadcrumbs stick to every part.
Ask an adult to help pour oil into a frying pan about 1cm deep and heat over medium heat until a breadcrumb sizzles right away.
Carefully lay the cutlet into the oil away from you. Fry 3-4 minutes until deep golden brown, then flip and fry the other side another 3-4 minutes.
Ask an adult to help lift the cutlet onto a wire rack or paper towels to drain, and let it rest 2 minutes.
Slice the cutlet into strips, pile the shredded cabbage next to it, and serve with steamed rice and tonkatsu sauce.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Salmon + Miso Soup
recipes.dish_alt: Glazed teriyaki salmon fillet glossy with sauce, served over rice
recipes.prep_alt: A bowl of miso soup with tofu and wakame seaweed

sections.heading: Steps
items: Bring water to a boil, stir in dashi granules, then turn heat to low. Add wakame and cubed tofu and let simmer gently while you start the salmon.
Stir together soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves — this is your teriyaki sauce.
Heat a splash of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Pat the salmon dry and lay it skin-side down. Cook 4 minutes undisturbed, then flip and cook 2-3 minutes more.
Pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan and spoon the bubbling glaze over the fish until glossy, about 1-2 more minutes.
Turn off the soup's heat completely, stir a spoonful of hot broth into the miso paste until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.
Ladle the miso soup into bowls and top with sliced green onion. Plate the glazed salmon over rice.

recipes.title: Gyoza (Pan-Fried Pork Dumplings)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden pan-fried gyoza dumplings with crispy bottoms served on a plate
recipes.prep_alt: Hands folding and pleating gyoza dumpling wrappers around filling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Sprinkle chopped cabbage with a pinch of salt, let sit 5 minutes, then squeeze out the extra water.
Mix the ground pork, squeezed cabbage, garlic, ginger, green onion, soy sauce, and sesame oil into an even filling.
Spoon about a teaspoon of filling into the center of a wrapper. Wet the edge, fold in half, and pinch 3-4 pleats to seal tightly.
Repeat with the rest of the filling and wrappers, keeping finished dumplings under a damp towel.
Heat oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Arrange dumplings standing up, flat-bottom down.
Fry undisturbed 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are deep golden brown.
Carefully pour in about 60ml water per batch of 8 and cover immediately — it will splatter loudly.
Steam 3-4 minutes until the water is mostly gone, then uncover and let the bottoms crisp back up for another minute.
Stir together the dipping soy sauce and rice vinegar and serve alongside the crisp-bottomed dumplings.

recipes.title: Oyakodon (Chicken & Egg Rice Bowl)
recipes.dish_alt: Oyakodon rice bowl with soft-set egg and chicken over steamed rice
recipes.prep_alt: Eggs being beaten in a bowl with a whisk

sections.heading: Steps
items: Stir together dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a shallow lidded pan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the sliced onion and cook 2-3 minutes until slightly see-through.
Add the chicken pieces in a single layer and simmer 4-5 minutes until no pink remains.
Beat the eggs lightly, leaving streaks of yolk and white visible.
Pour two-thirds of the egg over the chicken and onion in a swirl. Don't stir — let it sit on top.
Cover and cook undisturbed 30 seconds, then pour the rest of the egg into the gaps, cover, and cook 30-45 seconds more until just set and glossy.
Turn off the heat right away. Slide the chicken-and-egg mixture over a bowl of hot rice and sprinkle with green onion.

recipes.title: Japanese Chicken Curry Rice
recipes.dish_alt: Japanese chicken curry with carrots and potato ladled over steamed rice
recipes.prep_alt: Blocks of Japanese curry roux ready to melt into the simmering pot

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the sliced onion 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden.
Add the chicken and cook 3-4 minutes until the outside is no longer pink.
Add the carrot and potato and stir for 1 minute so they get lightly coated.
Pour in the water or stock, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Skim off any grey foam that rises to the surface.
Cover partway and simmer 15 minutes, until a fork slides easily into the potato and carrot.
Turn off the heat completely, break the curry roux into pieces, and drop them in.
Stir gently but thoroughly until every piece of roux has melted with no lumps.
Turn the heat back to low and simmer 5 more minutes, stirring often, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Serve the curry ladled over a bowl of steamed rice, plated side by side.

recipes.title: Sukiyaki (Beef & Vegetable Hot Pot)
recipes.dish_alt: Sukiyaki hot pot with beef, napa cabbage, tofu, and mushrooms simmering in a pan
recipes.prep_alt: Raw beef, napa cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu arranged on a platter before cooking

sections.heading: Steps
items: Stir together soy sauce, mirin, sugar, sake, and an equal amount of water until the sugar dissolves — this is the warishita sauce.
Boil the shirataki noodles 1-2 minutes to remove their odor, then drain.
Arrange the beef, cabbage, green onion, mushrooms, tofu, and noodles on a big platter, grouped by type.
Heat a wide, heavy pan over medium heat with a little oil or beef fat.
Lay a few slices of beef in the pan and sear 30-45 seconds per side until light brown outside.
Pour in about a third of the warishita sauce, then push the beef to one side.
Add the vegetables, tofu, and noodles to the empty side, pour in more sauce, and simmer gently 5-7 minutes until the cabbage softens.
Check the beef is fully cooked with no pink remaining.
If using, crack an egg into a small bowl and beat it for dipping.
Serve straight from the pot — everyone picks pieces with chopsticks, dips in egg if using, and tops up sauce and ingredients as things get eaten.

recipes.title: Shoyu Ramen (Soy Sauce Ramen)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of shoyu ramen with sliced pork, soft-boiled egg, nori, and green onion in soy-sauce broth
recipes.prep_alt: A soy-marinated soft-boiled egg with a jammy yolk, halved

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Sliced pork belly or chicken thigh

sections.heading: Steps
items: Lower the eggs gently into already-boiling water and time exactly 6½-7 minutes for a jammy yolk.
Transfer the eggs straight into ice water to stop cooking, then peel.
Marinate the peeled eggs in soy sauce and mirin at least 15 minutes.
Sear the sliced pork or chicken 2-3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Set aside.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer and stir in soy sauce, mirin, and minced garlic. Taste and adjust.
Boil the ramen noodles according to the package time, usually 2-4 minutes, until they bend easily but still have a slight bite.
Drain the noodles and twist them into a neat nest in each serving bowl.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles, filling each bowl about three-quarters full.
Slice the marinated eggs in half and arrange them with the pork or chicken, green onion, nori, and menma on top.
Serve immediately while the broth is hot and the noodles are still springy.

recipes.title: Dorayaki (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Dorayaki red bean pancake sandwiches stacked on a plate
recipes.prep_alt: A bowl of sweet red bean paste (anko) for filling the pancakes

sections.heading: Steps
items: Whisk the egg, sugar, and honey together for about a minute until pale yellow and slightly thick.
Sift the flour and baking powder into the bowl and gently fold in with a spatula, using a scooping motion.
Add the water or milk a little at a time, folding until the batter falls off the spatula in a slow ribbon. Let it rest 15 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over low-medium heat.
Pour a small ladle of batter to form a circle. Cook until bubbles appear all over and the edges look dry and matte, about 2 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook the other side about 1 minute until golden brown and springy.
Stack the cooked pancakes under a clean towel as you go to keep them soft.
Once cooled to warm, spread red bean paste on the flat side of one pancake and sandwich with another, flat sides facing in.
